facts.statement: The genus Angoumeius is named after its type locality in Angoumé, France.
facts.quote: It is named for its type locality, Angoumé, France.

facts.statement: Angoumeius is known from many isolated teeth found in the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: It is known from many isolated teeth from the Lutetian stage.

facts.statement: There are seven recorded fossil occurrences of Angoumeius.
The parent group of Angoumeius is the family Dalatiidae.
Angoumeius belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Angoumeius lived from the Danian to the Bartonian, spanning 66 to 37.71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Bartonian (66 to 37.71 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the unusual dentition of Angoumeius allows for a certain familial placement and relationship with other genera.
facts.quote: The inferred dentition is highly unusual for so its familial placement and relationship with other genera remains uncertain.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Angoumeius may be closely related to Kitefin or Sleeper sharks.
facts.quote: It may be close to Kitefin or Sleeper sharks.

rejected.statement: Angoumeius is an extinct genus of squaliform shark that lived during the Eocene epoch of the Paleogene period.
rejected.quote: It is an extinct genus of squaliform shark from the Eocene epoch of the Paleogene period.
